pairs: Et factum est verbum Domini ad me in anno nono,
And the word of the Lord came to me, in the ninth year,
on the tenth day of the month,
write for yourself the name of this day,
in qua confirmatus est rex Babylonis adversum Jerusalem hodie.
on which the king of Babylon was confirmed against Jerusalem today.
Et dices per proverbium ad domum irritatricem parabolam,
And you shall speak, through a proverb, a parable to the inciting house.
And you shall say to them:
I say, and put water into it.
Pile together within it every morsel,
the choice pieces and those full of bones.
Take the fattest from the flock,
compone quoque strues ossium sub ea:
and arrange also a heap of bones under it.
et discocta sunt ossa illius in medio ejus.
and its bones in its midst have been thoroughly cooked.
ollæ cujus rubigo in ea est,
Woe to the city of blood,
et rubigo ejus non exivit de ea!
to the cooking pot that has rust in it,
and whose rust has not gone out of it!
et per partes suas ejice eam:
Cast it out piece by piece!
No lot has fallen upon it.
Sanguis enim ejus in medio ejus est;
For her blood is in her midst;
she has shed it upon the smoothest rock.
She has not shed it upon the ground,
so that it could be covered with dust.
So shall I bring my indignation over her,
dedi sanguinem ejus super petram limpidissimam,
I have presented her blood upon the smoothest rock,
so that it would not be covered.
Because of this, thus says the Lord God:
Woe to the city of blood,
out of which I will make a great funeral pyre.
which I will burn with fire.
and the entire composition shall be boiled,
Pone quoque eam super prunas vacuam,
Also, place it empty on burning coals,
so that it may be heated,
et confletur in medio ejus inquinamentum ejus,
And let the filth of it be melted in its midst,
and let its rust be consumed.
There has been much sweat and labor,
et non exivit de ea nimia rubigo ejus,
and yet its extensive rust has not gone out of it,
For I wanted to cleanse you,
et non es mundata a sordibus tuis:
and you have not been cleansed from your filth.
donec quiescere faciam indignationem meam in te.
neither will you be cleansed before I cause my indignation over you to cease.
juxta vias tuas, et juxta adinventiones tuas judicabo te,
I will judge you according to your ways and according to your intentions,
Et factum est verbum Domini ad me,
And the word of the Lord came to me,
ecce ego tollo a te desiderabile oculorum tuorum in plaga:
I am taking away from you, with a stroke, the desire of your eyes.
And your tears shall not flow down.
you shall make no mourning for the dead.
Let the band of your crown be on you,
et calceamenta tua erunt in pedibus tuis:
and let your shoes be on your feet.
And you shall not cover your face,
nor shall you eat the food of those who mourn.”
Locutus sum ergo ad populum mane,
Therefore, I spoke to the people in the morning.
et mortua est uxor mea vespere:
And my wife died in the evening.
And in the morning, I did just as he had instructed me.
And the people said to me:
Quare non indicas nobis quid ista significent quæ tu facis?
“Why won’t you explain to us what these things signify, which you are doing?”
Sermo Domini factus est ad me,
“The word of the Lord came to me,
Behold, I will defile my sanctuary,
and the desire of your eyes,
et super quo pavet anima vestra:
and the dread of your soul.
filii vestri et filiæ vestræ quas reliquistis,
Your sons and your daughters, whom you have forsaken,
And so, you shall do just as I have done.
You shall not cover your faces,
and you shall not eat the food of those who mourn.
You shall have crowns on your heads,
et calceamenta in pedibus: non plangetis,
and shoes on your feet. You shall not lament,
Instead, you will waste away in your iniquities,
et unusquisque gemet ad fratrem suum.
and each one will groan to his brother.
Eritque Ezechiel vobis in portentum: juxta omnia quæ fecit,
‘And Ezekiel shall be a portent for you. In accord with all that he has done,
so shall you do, when this will happen.
et scietis quia ego Dominus Deus.
And you shall know that I am the Lord God.’”
ecce in die qua tollam ab eis fortitudinem eorum,
in the day when I will take away from them their strength,
and the joy of their dignity,
and the desire of their eyes,
in which their souls find rest:
cum venerit fugiens ad te ut annuntiet tibi:
when one who is fleeing will come to you, so that he may report to you,
aperietur os tuum cum eo qui fugit,
your mouth shall be opened to him who has fled.
and you shall no longer be silent.
And you shall be for them a portent.
And you shall know that I am the Lord.”
